👋 Hi! Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.
 Just a reminder: PRs would not trigger full CI run by default. Instead, it would only run `fastcheck` CI which starts running only a small and essential subset of CI tests to quickly catch errors. You can run other CI tests on top of those by going to your `fastcheck` build on Buildkite UI (linked in the PR checks section) and unblock them. If you do not have permission to unblock, ping `simon-mo` or `khluu` to add you in our Buildkite org. 

Once the PR is approved and ready to go, your PR reviewer(s) can run CI to test the changes comprehensively before merging.

 To run CI, PR reviewers can do one of these:
- Add `ready` label to the PR
- Enable auto-merge.

🚀

Thank you so much for your review.

> I prefer the unify approach, but have concerns about the untouch:
> 
> 1. It mark the untouched blocks as recent used, which is not right.

Strictly yes, but perhaps it does not hurt to mark these blocks because they are existentially most wanted blocks.
 
> 2. It introduces some overheads with long context, because you touch a long sequence of blocks and untouch them.

Right. There is pros and cons to this speculative touch-and-untouch-if-have-to approach. The positive side is that we don't need to calculate the num_evictable_computed_blocks (short and long) every time, which is arguably the 'normal' case, so the net outcome could still be positive.

Please feel free to choose either one, the untouch is reverted in the last commit.

Thanks.

> Otherwise LGTM. It's pretty clean now.

Thank you so much for your time.

nodes.body: This function breaks the LRU cache policy, because when you touch a block and untouch it, you moved the block to the end of the free queue. It means the block is "used" recently and is less likely evicted. However, In the case that we cannot allocate new blocks for a request, the computed blocks cannot be treat as "recent used".

nodes.body:
## Code Review 摘要

This PR cleanly unifies the prefill (allocate_slots) and decode (append_slots) paths into a single KVCacheManager.allocate_slots, and the block accounting (num_required_blocks - len(req_blocks) - len(new_computed_blocks) vs. the post-touch free-block count) is equivalent to the previous logic, so the refactor looks behaviorally sound and the test updates are reasonable. Two points to address: the touch-then-untouch ordering can perturb the free-queue/LRU eviction order on allocation failure instead of checking free capacity before touching, and a small comment typo (\"cacheing\"). Triage passed (208 counted changed lines, no breaking/RFC markers, no security core files), so this is an automated review.

**决策（policy）**: COMMENT

### 发现问题
- 🟡 medium: 1
- 🟢 low: 1

🟡 **bug** (medium)

allocate_slots now touches the new computed blocks (incrementing ref_cnt and removing evictable ones from the free queue) at the very top, before the free-block availability check. When the check fails it reverses this with _untouch. But FreeKVCacheBlockQueue.append re-inserts blocks at the tail (most-recently-used position) and the queue's eviction order relies on blocks being re-appended in reverse order for a chain. Re-appending the prefix-cache blocks on failure therefore loses their original LRU position/chain order, so under memory pressure the LRU eviction order is perturbed - blocks that should be evicted first may survive while fresher cached prefixes get evicted. It also adds an extra queue mutation on every failed allocation.

**建议**: Perform the free-block check (num_new_blocks > self.free_block_queue.num_free_blocks) before calling self._touch(...), and touch the computed blocks only after the allocation is known to succeed. That makes _untouch unnecessary and avoids ever disturbing the free-queue order. (This is also the direction the PR later took in follow-up commits.)

**证据**: `            self._untouch(new_computed_blocks)`

inline_comments.body: This function breaks the LRU cache policy, because when you touch a block and untouch it, you moved the block to the end of the free queue. It means the block is "used" recently and is less likely evicted. However, In the case that we cannot allocate new blocks for a request, the computed blocks cannot be treat as "recent used".

inline_comments.body:
🟡 **bug** (medium)

allocate_slots now touches the new computed blocks (incrementing ref_cnt and removing evictable ones from the free queue) at the very top, before the free-block availability check. When the check fails it reverses this with _untouch. But FreeKVCacheBlockQueue.append re-inserts blocks at the tail (most-recently-used position) and the queue's eviction order relies on blocks being re-appended in reverse order for a chain. Re-appending the prefix-cache blocks on failure therefore loses their original LRU position/chain order, so under memory pressure the LRU eviction order is perturbed - blocks that should be evicted first may survive while fresher cached prefixes get evicted. It also adds an extra queue mutation on every failed allocation.

**建议**: Perform the free-block check (num_new_blocks > self.free_block_queue.num_free_blocks) before calling self._touch(...), and touch the computed blocks only after the allocation is known to succeed. 🚀

Thank you so much for your review.

> I prefer the unify approach, but have concerns about the untouch:
> 
> 1. It mark the untouched blocks as recent used, which is not right.

Strictly yes, but perhaps it does not hurt to mark these blocks because they are existentially most wanted blocks.
 
> 2. It introduces some overheads with long context, because you touch a long sequence of blocks and untouch them.

Right. There is pros and cons to this speculative touch-and-untouch-if-have-to approach. The positive side is that we don't need to calculate the num_evictable_computed_blocks (short and long) every time, which is arguably the 'normal' case, so the net outcome could still be positive.

Please feel free to choose either one, the untouch is reverted in the last commit.

Thanks.

> Otherwise LGTM. It's pretty clean now.

Thank you so much for your time.
@WoosukKwon PTAL if you got a chance. Will merge the PR once CI is passed (or force merge if needed).

reviews.body:
I prefer the unify approach, but have concerns about the untouch:
1. It mark the untouched blocks as recent used, which is not right.
2. It introduces some overheads with long context, because you touch a long sequence of blocks and untouch them.
Otherwise LGTM. It's pretty clean now.

## Code Review 摘要

This PR cleanly unifies the prefill (allocate_slots) and decode (append_slots) paths into a single KVCacheManager.allocate_slots, and the block accounting (num_required_blocks - len(req_blocks) - len(new_computed_blocks) vs. the post-touch free-block count) is equivalent to the previous logic, so the refactor looks behaviorally sound and the test updates are reasonable. Two points to address: the touch-then-untouch ordering can perturb the free-queue/LRU eviction order on allocation failure instead of checking free capacity before touching, and a small comment typo (\"cacheing\").
